episodes.summary: All week this show has been asking a version of the same question. Are private credit's own numbers honest? We've walked through a default statistic that turns out to be elective, non-accruals at a post-2017 high, and a record default rate built on maturity extensions rather than actual payment failure.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — September 17, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the terms, straight from the company's own filing. The Baldwin Group, the insurance broker, is going private for thirty-two dollars and fifty cents a share in cash. That values the business at about seven point seven billion dollars of enterprise value.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — September 17, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop. Strategic Power reads the hike as forced rather than chosen. US diesel is at a record six dollars and twenty-seven cents a gallon, and the damaged Saudi pipeline to Yanbu now carries a five-to-six-week repair estimate, from a secondary tracker rather than from Aramco.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — September 17, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard, because two calls resolved yesterday afternoon. I said the committee raises rates by a quarter point on September sixteenth, and I carried that at roughly four-in-five. It landed.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — September 18, 2026
episodes.summary: On five separate sessions this month, this show has logged the same fact about xAI: no model card, no benchmark, no context window, no price. We logged it again on Wednesday. Today that pattern doesn't break so much as relocate. The capability didn't show up in a document. It showed up in customers' cars.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — September 18, 2026
episodes.summary: The first Fed hike since 2023 landed Wednesday afternoon. It was a quarter point, taking the target range to three and three-quarters to four percent, and it reversed the cutting cycle that came before it. The sting wasn't the size. It was a committee that now projects more to come, which we'll get to.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — September 18, 2026
episodes.summary: On Wednesday this beat argued, from wafer-allocation ratios alone, that the AI memory shortage now functions as an input-cost tax on the rest of electronics. Today that tax has a price attached. And the capacity that eventually ends it has acquired a date.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — September 18, 2026
episodes.summary: Two days ago, this briefing described Anthropic as buying distribution the slow way. The read was that Anthropic was pushing its agentic Cowork workspace onto more surfaces, web and mobile, one platform at a time. That read is now wrong. On September 16th, Anthropic deleted the surface entirely.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — September 18, 2026
episodes.summary: We start with the hardest dollar figure enterprise tech has produced in weeks, and it is an outflow. Oracle's own quarterly filing with the SEC, for the quarter ended August 31st, states that its 2026 restructuring plan carries total estimated costs of up to $2.1 billion as of quarter-end.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — September 18, 2026
episodes.summary: For eight sessions running, this beat has asked the same question of every humanoid vendor: show us a controlled number, not a demo. Yesterday we said plainly that nobody had shown Figure's video-pretraining data actually improves its robot's fielded success rate.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — September 18, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with Rocket Lab and Iridium. On September 15th, Rocket Lab said it had fully funded the cash portion of its acquisition of Iridium, a deal worth roughly 8 billion dollars of enterprise value.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — September 18, 2026
episodes.summary: Five straight sessions on this desk have argued the same thing. Private credit is getting worse at the bottom of the stack. A record default rate, non-accruals at a post-2017 high, a Blue Owl mark that went from near par to pennies inside two quarters. Today's news does not dispute any of that.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — September 18, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with Blackstone, because it's the cleanest instance this week of a pattern worth naming directly. Bloomberg reported yesterday that Blackstone is in conversations with potential buyers to arrange a secondary sale.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — September 18, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop, and with Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar, because everything else on today's tape traces back to it.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — September 18, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard, and the call that moved hardest against me. Yesterday I reversed my oil view and said front-month Brent does not close below a hundred dollars a barrel before the end of October, at roughly seven-in-ten.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — September 19, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the document everything this week turns on. On September 12, Anthropic's chief executive Dario Amodei published an essay arguing that the industry must slow the pace at which it improves AI capabilities. His central ask was concrete.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — September 19, 2026
episodes.summary: The number that moved most this week was not the funds rate. It was the probability attached to a meeting that has not happened yet. The Fed hiked on Wednesday, unanimously. By Thursday, a relay of the CME's FedWatch gauge had an October hike at a coin flip. By Friday morning, CNBC put it near 58 percent.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — September 19, 2026
episodes.summary: Three sessions ago, this show said the crypto sector had lost its irreversibility when the CLARITY Act died in the Senate. We also said the idea that agencies would fill the gap was industry expectation, not evidence. This week supplied the evidence. The SEC and the CFTC redrew the perimeter inside forty-eight hours.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — September 19, 2026
episodes.summary: I have to correct our own framing this week. This beat called Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the line that carries crude across the kingdom to Yanbu on the Red Sea, bypassing Hormuz, the kingdom's single remaining point of failure. On Thursday we said to watch whether it came back inside its repair window.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — September 19, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's story starts with a number that costs its author something. Nvidia's gross margin is heading down, and the stated reason is what it pays for memory. Almost every large figure on this beat comes from a party that benefits from it. This one does not.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — September 19, 2026
episodes.summary: This week, the product news stopped being about which assistant you talk to. It became about who owns the corpus underneath the assistant, and where the meter sits behind the flat-rate plan. We start with the corpus.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — September 19, 2026
episodes.summary: The most useful number in enterprise AI this month did not come from a keynote. It came from an invoice. On September 1st, GitHub's promotional Copilot credits expired. The included usage per seat dropped, and the seat price stayed exactly where it was.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — September 19, 2026
episodes.summary: Capital in this field has been pricing AI capability rather than proof, and stacking the money upstream at discovery and design. Today one sponsor bought both halves of the capability trade in forty-eight hours. And for the first time, a large institutional check landed on the plumbing instead of the models.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — September 19, 2026
episodes.summary: Humanoid vendors will not publish a fielded-reliability number. No intervention rate, no uptime, no cost per completed task. This week a number arrived anyway, and it came from outside the vendors entirely. It came as a share price, and it went down.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — September 19, 2026
episodes.summary: This week the thing to watch was not a launch. It was a contract structure. The US government is buying an outcome instead of a satellite count, and that changes where value accrues in orbit.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — September 19, 2026
episodes.summary: The most useful thing that happened this week is a sale where the money came from outside private equity. H.I.G. Capital agreed to sell General Datatech, known as GDT, to the London-listed reseller Softcat, at an enterprise value of one point zero five billion dollars. H.I.G. has owned GDT since 2021.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — September 19, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop, and with Strategic Power, because the oil story is the assumption under everything else. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline is still down, but the repair window has stopped being the variable that matters.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — September 19, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard, and start with the call that went against me. On Thursday I said Salesforce would attach no published dollar rate to its seven named production agents before its next earnings call, and yesterday I marked that up to about four-in-five.
